simple.meaning: בָּדָא (bâdâʼ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “(figuratively) to invent.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in 1 Kings, Nehemiah, beginning at 1 Kings 12:33. The surrounding contexts include altar, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּדָא (H908) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: בָּדָא (bâdâʼ) / H908 is traced through 1 Kings 12:33, Nehemiah 6:8 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He went up to the altar which he had made in Bethel on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, even in the month which he had devised of his own heart; and he ordained a feast for the children of Israel, and went up to the altar, to burn incense.

timeline.evidenceText: He went up to the altar which he had made in Bethel on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, even in the month which he had devised of his own heart; and he ordained a feast for the children of Israel, and went up to the altar, to burn incense.
Then I sent to him, saying, “There are no such things done as you say, but you imagine them out of your own heart.”

definitions.full: H908. bada בָּדָא verb devise, invent (bad sense) (Mishna id. , Aramaic בְּדָא , invent ; compare Arabic begin, make a beginning — Qal Perfect בָּדָא 1Kin 12:33 ; Participle suffix בּוֺדָאם (instead of בּוֺדְאָם ) Neh 6:8 — Jeroboam devised a feast in 8th month 1Kin 12:33 ; invent accusation Neh 6:8 .
